name: Analog Devices
fiscalYearEnd: 52/53-week year ending on the Saturday nearest October 31 (EDGAR fiscal-year-end 1031; FY2025 ended 2025-11-01)
description: Analog Devices designs high-performance analog, mixed-signal and power chips that convert real-world signals (sound, temperature, pressure, light, radio) into data, and sells several thousand products, many with hundreds of end customers each. It is one reporting segment, described by end market: industrial (45 percent of FY2025 revenue), automotive (30), consumer (13) and communications (13). More than half the wafers come from outside foundries, with own fabs in Massachusetts, Washington, Oregon and Ireland. A majority (56 percent) of revenue goes through distributors. Revenue grew 40 percent year on year in the quarter ended 2026-08-01, led by industrial and communications.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label as shown on Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (columns GICS Sector and GICS Sub-Industry). That page does not show the industry group or industry, so those are null rather than filled from memory.

hq.note: One Analog Way, Wilmington, MA 01887 (FY2025 10-K cover); incorporated in Massachusetts

employees.note: About 24,500 employees, about 13,000 in engineering roles (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Industrial
businessLines.how: Chips sold per unit, largely through distributors, into long-lived industrial designs; revenue follows industrial capital spending and customer inventory cycles.
businessLines.description: Instrumentation, automation, healthcare, aerospace and defense, energy, and related equipment.

businessLines.name: Automotive
businessLines.how: Chips sold per unit to car makers and Tier 1 suppliers, typically designed in years ahead of production and shipped through the model life.
businessLines.description: Vehicle electrification, in-cabin and safety/connectivity chips.

businessLines.name: Consumer
businessLines.how: Chips sold per unit into consumer electronics; more seasonal and volume driven.
businessLines.description: Wearables, smartphones and other consumer devices.

businessLines.name: Communications
businessLines.how: Chips sold per unit to network and infrastructure equipment makers.
businessLines.description: Wired and wireless infrastructure, data center, satellite communications.
